### Where the full Telegram history actually lives

Named by `HR-735` as a place to check before asking him anything. The honest
answer is that **no single complete transcript exists in this repository**, so
check in this order:

1. `instance/decisions/triage.jsonl` — the only tracked, complete-by-intent record
   of his words. One row per triaged message, quote included.
2. `instance/decisions/HR-*.md` — the rulings, in full, where a message decided
   something.
3. `~/.claude/channels/telegram/history/messages-YYYY-MM.jsonl` — host-only, and
   **metadata only**: timestamps, direction, outcome, length and a content hash.
   The message text is not there. Retention and size caps are set in
   `daemon/history-logger.ts`, so old months are deleted on their own.
4. The v1 orchestrator, which holds the older history: reach it through the file
   channel in `instance/channels.md`, not through the branch that looks like it.

If a question survives all four, it is genuinely unanswered and `HR-735` permits
asking it.

## Facts about this installation

- `instance/params.yaml` — the parameter file, and the one home for every value in it. 8 sections: `operator`, `phase`, `repos`, `vm`, `fleet`, `orchestrator`, `capture`, `db`. Values are deliberately not copied here; a fact with two homes is a fact that drifts.
- `instance/required-mechanisms.tsv` and `instance/expected-mechanisms.tsv` — two independently maintained inventories of what must exist: 21 systemd units, 6 checkers, plus the gate, the cron and the runners. `tools/check-mechanism-reachability.ts` refuses when they disagree, when a target is missing, or when a mechanism nothing can reach is still listed.
- `instance/expected-units.tsv` with `instance/units/*.in` and `bootstrap/units/*.in` — the unit templates this host renders, pinned independently so deleting a template cannot shrink the truth. `bootstrap/check-unit-drift.sh` compares rendered units against the installed ones.
- `instance/packs.conf`, `instance/tags.conf` — which instruction docs each role's mission pack carries.
- `instance/workboard.md` — the live board: every row, its acceptance, and its state.

The checkers that enumerate and verify parts of this installation:

- `tools/check-decision-ledger-drift.sh`
- `tools/check-github-ref-protection.sh`
- `hygiene/check-shared-stash.sh`
- `tools/check-mechanism-reachability.ts`
- `tools/check-documented-mission-cli.ts`
- `hygiene/check-retained-branches.ts`

**Not yet true, and stated here rather than implied:** there is no complete
enumeration of the non-git host state — the state database, mission and lane
history, durable evidence outside this tree. That is workboard row **V3-2.9**, open.
Until it exists, this section indexes what the repository knows about itself, not
everything the host holds.

## Credentials — which exist, and where they live

From `instance/credentials.tsv`. **Locations, identities and purposes only — never
a value.** This is the section that exists so the question stops being asked; the
required scope, the rotation procedure and a verification command per credential
are workboard row **V3-2.10**, still open.

| credential | location | identity | purpose | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `github-ssh` | `/root/.ssh/id_github_vova` | - | SSH key this box uses for the GitHub remote named in params.yaml (repos.git_remote); the public half sits beside it | operator, at VM setup 2026-07-30 |
| `github-api-token` | `environment GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN` | - | REST credential tools/check-github-ref-protection.sh needs to read branch protection; when it is absent the checker fails closed with reason=credential-missing | NOT provisioned on this host |
| `google-service-account` | `/root/.config/bpa/oauth/gcp-sa-bpapro-agents.json` | bpa-dev-orch@bpapro-agents.iam.gserviceaccount.com (project bpapro-agents) | the machine's OWN Google Drive identity, as distinct from the interactive Drive connection on an orchestrator session (HR-2171); a Drive folder must be shared TO this address for the operator to see what it writes, and it must never be backed up to the Drive it authenticates to | operator, before 2026-08-04 |
| `google-oauth-client` | `/root/.config/bpa/oauth/google.env` | - | OAuth client id and secret for the PRODUCT's Google integration; not used by the control plane | operator |
| `qbo-oauth-client` | `/root/.config/bpa/oauth/qbo.env` | - | OAuth client id and secret plus environment/realm hint for the PRODUCT's QuickBooks integration; not used by the control plane | operator |
| `claude-login` | `/root/.claude/.credentials.json` | - | Claude provider subscription login; the launch preflight reads it structurally via ORCH_CLAUDE_CRED_FILE and refuses to start when it does not prove subscription login | interactive login |
| `codex-login` | `/root/.codex/auth.json` | owned by the bpa service user, not root | Codex provider subscription login; the launch preflight reads it structurally via ORCH_CODEX_AUTH_FILE | interactive `codex login` as that user |
| `telegram-bot` | `orchestrator/runtime.env` | - | bot token and chat binding the Telegram daemon runs on; gitignored by design, its tracked contract is orchestrator/runtime.env.example and its install-time placeholder is bootstrap/env.template | operator paste at install |
| `legacy-orchestrator-env` | `/root/.config/bpa/orchestrator.env` | - | the v1 control plane's environment file, still named as ENV_FILE by every rendered systemd unit (bootstrap/unit-render-lib.sh); its .bak-20260730 sibling is known to be secret-bearing and must not leave this host | legacy, predates v3 |
